item.title: Solved: Can a Website Detect When You Are Using Selenium with ChromeDriver?
item.description:
Solved: Can a Website Detect When You Are Using Selenium with ChromeDriver?

When it comes to web scraping and automation, using Selenium with ChromeDriver often raises the question of whether it can be detected by websites designed to identify automated browsing. My own experiments have shown that while browsing websites through Selenium, encounters with suspicious activity warnings are common—despite using settings that replicate normal browser behavior.

In my trials, I was able to browse normally when using the Chrome browser directly, but faced blocks and redirect warnings as soon as I switched to Selenium. Understanding how websites detect Selenium usage is crucial for anyone looking to scrape data without raising alarms. Here are some strategies and solutions for evading detection:

item.title: Top 12 Methods to Solve the 'chromedriver' Executable Needs to Be Available in the Path Error
item.description:
Solving the ‘chromedriver’ Executable Needs to Be Available in the Path Error

Encountering the error message stating that the 'chromedriver' executable needs to be available in the path can be frustrating when automating tasks with Selenium and Python. This issue typically arises when the system cannot locate the ChromeDriver executable, which is essential for running Chrome in a Selenium environment. Below, we explore twelve effective methods to troubleshoot and resolve this common issue.
